biodiversity_overview.text: 4,158 GBIF occurrence records for 48 tracked species are attributed to Jharkhand, spanning 1899-2026.
4,113 of these records (98.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 25, Magnoliopsida 10, Mammalia 6, Squamata 3, Amphibia 2, Testudines 1, Actinopterygii 1.

threatened_species.text: 4 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
1 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (767), Indian Cuckoo-shrike (759), Indian Cuckoo (334), Indian Pitta (304), Indian Golden Oriole (251).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 25 in 2016 to 6 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 2.76% of Jharkhand's area (13 areas intersect the state).
14.8% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (608 of 4,113); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Eastern Indian Leopard Gecko (0.47), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Indian Red Wood (0.33).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Jharkhand (equal-weight reference): cell near 23.625N 85.125E (overall rank 145, median rank across weightings 148); cell near 22.875N 85.125E (overall rank 297, median rank across weightings 302); cell near 24.375N 87.375E (overall rank 370, median rank across weightings 352).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 5,607 km2 (7.09% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

62.8 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (1.12% of the 2000 extent; 0.36% in 2015-2024, rank 21 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2009 (8.38 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.04% of land and population density is 494.4 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
51% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
